inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted diluted shares, Q2 2026 10-Q (112M; FY2025 113M). Held FLAT: SBC plus equity-award withholding taxes are fully expensed in the flows, and Quest funds the flat count with buybacks ($450M FY2025, $102M H1 2026), so charging dilution as well would double-count.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: stock-based compensation add-back $88M plus $45M taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards (financing activities). Quest publishes no combined SBC figure in its adjusted-EPS reconciliation (it does not exclude SBC), so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10y UST ~4.3%, beta ~0.65 (defensive healthcare services), ERP 5.0% -> cost of equity ~7.6%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (~4.1% after tax); market-value weights ~84% equity (~$26.5B cap) / 16% debt ($5.65B) -> ~7.0%. Rounded up to 7.5% for reimbursement/regulatory concentration (Medicare CLFS/PAMA). Same WACC in all three scenarios: risk is carried by the scenario weights, not stacked in the rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP ASC 842: operating lease cost sits inside operating expenses, so EBITDA is already post-lease; operating lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt (one treatment). Finance leases are within total debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of EBITDA). Noncontrolling interests (~$44M/yr FY2025: consolidated NI $1,046M vs attributable ~$1,002M = EPS 8.87 x ~113M) are deducted in the equity bridge at ~15x. Equity-method JV earnings sit below operating income and are excluded from the flows; their carrying value is not added back (conservative, small).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 1: US operating company - clinical laboratory testing services, ~$11B revenue, stable margins; not a bank/REIT/holdco). First valuation of DGX (no MEMORY entry). Horizon 10 years. EBITDA is built PRE-SBC (FY2025 GAAP EBITDA $2,126M = operating income $1,556M + D&A $570M, + SBC $88M = $2,214M, 20.1% of revenue; H1 2026 20.1%) so SBC is charged exactly once in the flows. D&A includes acquired-intangible amortisation (tax deductible for asset deals), so D&A% glides down toward capex% by the terminal year to avoid perpetuating an amortisation tax shield. Cash tax: FY2025 cash taxes $169M were depressed by 2025 US tax law restoring 100% bonus depreciation and domestic R&D expensing (FY2023 $317M, FY2024 $256M); the unlevered rate ramps 21% -> 24%. Working capital: receivables-heavy business (payer billing), so growth consumes cash - negative capture on the revenue change (-6%: receivables ~12% of revenue less payables/accruals ~6%). Terminal caps: 15x base (structurally slow grower; Gordon at 7.5%/2.5% would be 20.5x), 17x bull, 12x bear. Price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print. Guidance: no filing text was extracted for this XBRL-only build; FY2026 year-1 growth is anchored to H1 2026 revenue +9.7% YoY (acquired outreach books incl. Fresenius/Spectra, Corewell, LifeLabs lapping) moderating in H2 to ~+7.5% for the year. Buybacks are real (FY2021-25 cumulative $4.5B), so the flat count is funded, not a convention.

equity_bridge.note: ~$44M/yr NCI share of consolidated NI (FY2025) x 15x; deducted because flows are 100% consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: 2019-2025 revenue CAGR 6.1% (pre-COVID base to post-COVID, includes tuck-in M&A of ~2pp/yr) haircut toward organic ~3-4%
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All 3- and 5-year CAGRs are distorted by the FY2020-22 COVID-testing windfall (revenue peaked $10.8B FY2021, fell to $9.3B FY2023). Equity 5yr CAGR 1.1% vs EPS -3.5% and revenue 3.2% (>30% divergence) - buybacks of $3.6B in FY2021-22 depressed book value. The pre-COVID-anchored 2019-2025 window is the meaningful comparison.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes (interest income immaterial; company is net debt). Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported FCF closely: SBC is only ~1.2% of revenue and is not outgrowing cash flow.

base.narrative: Mid-single-digit growth from volume, outreach-book acquisitions and advanced diagnostics; Invigorate automation offsets wage and reimbursement pressure for ~1pp of margin over five years.

scenario_narratives.base: Quest keeps compounding as the national consolidator of hospital outreach labs: FY2026 lands ~+7.5% on acquired books, then growth settles at 4-5% (2-3% organic volume/mix, 1-2pp tuck-ins) fading to 3%. PAMA Medicare clinical-lab-fee cuts are either delayed again or absorbed (Medicare CLFS is a mid-single-digit share of revenue). Invigorate automation and AI-driven revenue-cycle savings (~3%/yr of cost base) roughly offset wage inflation, so pre-SBC EBITDA margin creeps from 20.1% to 21%. Capex stays elevated near 4.5% of revenue as labs are automated.
scenario_narratives.bull: Advanced diagnostics (brain health/AD blood tests, oncology MRD, consumer-initiated testing) and a steady cadence of health-system outreach deals push growth to 6-8% for three years; PAMA is permanently reformed (SALSA-style) removing the reimbursement overhang; automation drives margin back toward the ~22-23% pre-COVID-peak range. Buybacks and a 3%+ dividend continue, with leverage staying ~2.5x.
scenario_narratives.bear: PAMA cuts of up to 15% per code finally take effect in 2027 and commercial payers follow Medicare's lead, Labcorp and hospital systems compete harder on price for outreach books, and wage/courier costs outrun productivity. Growth collapses to ~2% after the FY2026 acquisition lift and pre-SBC EBITDA margin falls to 18.5% (the FY2023-24 trough level). Terminal multiple compressed to 12x for an ex-growth, price-taker lab.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised to 25% from the 15% default because a single regulator (CMS, via the repeatedly deferred PAMA fee-schedule cuts) sets a benchmark price commercial payers reference; base 50% on a long record of stable mid-single-digit growth; bull cut to 25% because it needs advanced-diagnostics adoption, PAMA reform and margin expansion to all go right.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Quest is a mature, cash-generative US clinical lab consolidator. Value rests on durable volumes and a measured margin creep rather than growth; owner FCF charges SBC and award-withholding taxes, holds the share count flat, and deducts net debt and capitalised NCI. Reimbursement policy is the dominant swing factor, carried by the 25% bear weight rather than a WACC premium.
key_risks_to_valuation: PAMA / Medicare Clinical Lab Fee Schedule cuts (deferred repeatedly; could bite from 2027)
Commercial payer rate pressure and utilisation-management denials
Competition from Labcorp and hospital systems for outreach lab books; acquisition price inflation
Wage and logistics inflation outrunning automation savings
Leverage (~2.4x net debt/EBITDA) constrains buybacks if M&A continues
Cyber/IT incidents (2019 AMCA billing-vendor breach precedent)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 171.18-248.84
data_sources.financials: SEC XBRL (10-K FY2006-FY2025, 10-Q through Q2 2026) via DGX_Metrics.csv / DGX.duckdb; balance sheet at 30 June 2026
